narr: A strong and slow moving area of low pressure moved from the Central Plains on the 12th to over Minnesota on the morning of the 14th and became occluded. A cold front pushed across northwest Wisconsin on the 13th with heavy rainfall being received in some locations. Rainfall totals or 2-3 inches were recorded around Washburn County with most falling in a 5 hour period. Additionally, frost was still in the ground leading to higher than normal runoff rates. This lead to isolated minor flooding of ditches along with a few shoulder and road washouts in the Washburn County area. The worst damage was two large culvert pipes that were washed out in Barronett causing damage to a road as well. Additionally, a school bus in Price County tried to drive through a flooded roadway and became stuck as the shoulder gave way underneath it.
ev: A school bus became stranded in flood waters when the shoulder washed out underneath it and it partially tipped. Four students and the driver were helped from the bus to safety and there were no injuries reported, although the bus driver was taken to the hospital to be checked out. The bus went through the flooded section of road 15 minutes prior to returning and trying to make it through a second time.
